blocks.content: Quiz: Why doesn't fetch() automatically throw an error when the server responds with a 404 or 500 status?
Tap an option below to answer:
The catch block automatically catches 404 and 500 responses
The catch block only runs when the Promise rejects or when you throw — a 404 response does neither without a res.ok check.
The catch block only runs when the Promise rejects or when you throw — a 404 response does neither without a res.ok check.
fetch() always throws for any status above 200
fetch() is designed to resolve for all HTTP responses regardless of status.
fetch() is designed to resolve for all HTTP responses regardless of status.
You need to use axios instead of fetch() to detect error status codes
axios does throw for error status codes, but fetch() can handle it too — you just check res.ok yourself.
axios does throw for error status codes, but fetch() can handle it too — you just check res.ok yourself.
fetch() only rejects on network failures
The Promise resolves as long as a response was received, even if it's an error status. Checking the status is your responsibility.
The Promise resolves as long as a response was received, even if it's an error status. Checking the status is your responsibility.
